one_liner: Decompose any domain gap into photometric, geometric, and semantic components with controlled re-rendering - then publish the composition per benchmark.
problem: 'Domain gap' is treated as a scalar, but its composition (color/sensor vs viewpoint/layout vs class-distribution differences) determines which adaptation method can possibly work - and no benchmark reports its composition.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: using controlled transformations (photometric transplants, geometry-preserving style transfer, label-distribution reweighting), each popular shift benchmark decomposes into stable component fractions; adaptation methods' gains align with the component they address (photometric methods win only on photometric-heavy gaps), explaining most of the notorious inconsistency of UDA results across benchmarks.
why_important: Gives the field a diagnostic vocabulary: measure your gap's composition first, then choose methods - replacing the current lottery.
why_possibly_novel: Systematic gap-composition accounting across benchmarks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Build the three controlled transforms, measure component fractions on 6 shift pairs, correlate method-gain profiles with compositions.
main_risk: Components interact (not perfectly separable); report interaction terms honestly.

one_liner: Sim2real gap lives in materials, not geometry: hybrid renders (real textures on synthetic geometry, and vice versa) isolate what synthetic data gets wrong.
problem: Synthetic training data underperforms real data for segmentation, but WHERE the deficit lives (shape/layout realism vs material/lighting appearance) is folklore, not measurement - though it determines where rendering effort should go.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: crossing the factors (synthetic geometry + real-photograph textures vs real geometry + synthetic materials) shows the material/appearance factor explains the large majority of the sim2real segmentation gap, geometry realism contributing little - implying cheap geometry with photo-real materials is the optimal synthetic-data recipe, opposite to where most rendering compute goes.
why_important: Synthetic data budgets are large and misallocated if the geometry-heavy intuition is wrong; factor attribution redirects the spend.
why_possibly_novel: Factor-crossed hybrid rendering attribution for dense prediction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Construct the 2x2 render conditions in a driving simulator with texture transplants, train per cell, evaluate on real benchmarks.
main_risk: Texture transplantation introduces its own artifacts; needs artifact-matched controls.

one_liner: Night failure is mostly ISP failure: models degrade on processed JPEGs, not on darkness itself - RAW-domain evaluation separates the two.
problem: Nighttime segmentation failure is attributed to insufficient light, but consumer ISP pipelines (denoising, tone mapping, white balance) transform night captures aggressively and variably; models may fail on ISP artifacts rather than photon scarcity.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: evaluating on RAW-processed-with-fixed-simple-pipeline night images recovers a substantial fraction of the day-night performance drop relative to camera-ISP JPEGs (the ISP is a major failure contributor), and the recovered fraction varies by ISP vendor - night robustness research is partly chasing vendor-specific artifacts.
why_important: If the ISP is a first-order factor, night perception should be co-designed with capture pipelines, and existing night benchmarks measure entangled camera stacks rather than vision capability.
why_possibly_novel: ISP-vs-photon attribution for night dense prediction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Use datasets with RAW night captures (or collect paired RAW/JPEG), evaluate models across processing pipelines, decompose the drop.
main_risk: RAW night data with segmentation GT is scarce; may need targeted collection with transfer-annotated labels.

one_liner: Camera ISP fingerprint as an unbenchmarked shift axis: same scenes through different phone pipelines measurably move dense predictions.
problem: Every camera brand applies proprietary processing (sharpening, denoising, color science). Models trained on one ISP mix may silently degrade on another - an axis orthogonal to weather/geography that no benchmark isolates.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: capturing identical scenes with multiple devices (tripod-locked) and evaluating fixed models shows per-model prediction shifts comparable in magnitude to mild weather shift, with boundary-level metrics most affected (sharpening halos) - ISP variation is a first-class shift axis deserving its own benchmark. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search on existing cross-device studies.
why_important: Deployments span device fleets; an ignored first-order shift axis means fleet-wide QA is currently blind to a real variance source.
why_possibly_novel: Tripod-locked cross-ISP dense-prediction benchmarking appears missing.
minimal_experiment: Capture 200 locked scenes with 5 devices, run model zoo, quantify prediction divergence and metric movement per device pair.
main_risk: Perfect pixel alignment across devices is impossible (optics differ); evaluate with alignment-tolerant metrics.

one_liner: BN-statistics adaptation helps photometric shift but actively harms semantic shift: map when the cheapest TTA trick becomes poison.
problem: Test-time normalization-statistics adaptation is the default cheap fix under shift, applied indiscriminately; its failure conditions (when target statistics differences reflect content, not style) are anecdotal.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: across a controlled shift taxonomy, statistics adaptation improves photometric/sensor shifts consistently but DEGRADES performance under label-distribution and content shifts (it 'corrects' real signal), with the harm predictable from the correlation between channel statistics and class evidence - yielding a practical pre-test that decides whether to adapt.
why_important: A deploy-time go/no-go test for the most-used adaptation trick prevents silent self-inflicted damage.
why_possibly_novel: Shift-type-conditional harm characterization with a predictive pre-test is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Apply statistics adaptation across shift-type ladders (photometric, weather, geographic, class-mix), measure signed effects, validate the harm predictor.
main_risk: Modern normalization-free architectures reduce the scope; include them for completeness.

one_liner: Geographic shift decomposes into stuff-appearance and thing-longtail: cross-region failure has two mechanisms needing opposite remedies.
problem: Models trained in one region degrade in another, but the degradation conflates two mechanisms - unfamiliar background appearance (road surfaces, vegetation) and unfamiliar object variants (vehicle types, dress) - which respond to different fixes (style adaptation vs data collection).
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-class cross-region degradation splits bimodally - stuff classes fail by appearance statistics (fixable by style-level adaptation, no new labels) while thing classes fail by variant novelty (fixable only by target-region examples) - and the split predicts which classes any adaptation method can rescue, explaining heterogeneous published UDA results class-by-class.
why_important: Region expansion is the standard deployment problem (driving, agriculture, mapping); a mechanism-level failure map converts adaptation from alchemy to engineering.
why_possibly_novel: Mechanism-split analysis of geographic shift per class is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Cross-evaluate on multi-region datasets (Mapillary regions, IDD vs Cityscapes), classify per-class failures by style-transfer-recoverability, validate the two-mechanism model.
main_risk: Some classes fail by both mechanisms; use continuous mixture attribution, not hard split.

one_liner: Transferability is spatially structured: sky transfers, road texture does not - build per-region transfer maps and adapt only what fails.
problem: Adaptation methods treat images uniformly, but shift affects scene regions unequally (sky is universal; ground textures are local). Spatially-selective adaptation could preserve what already transfers - if transfer geography were measured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-pixel cross-domain performance retention has strong reproducible spatial/semantic structure (a transfer map stable across model families), uniform adaptation methods measurably damage well-transferring regions while fixing bad ones (netting less than possible), and transfer-map-gated adaptation beats uniform adaptation at matched compute.
why_important: Reveals adaptation's hidden collateral damage and provides a general recipe (measure, gate, adapt) applicable to every UDA method.
why_possibly_novel: Transfer-geography mapping with gated adaptation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Compute per-class/per-region retention across 4 shift pairs and 3 models, verify map stability, implement gated variant of one standard UDA method.
main_risk: Gating needs target labels to validate - use held-out target labels for science, proxy signals for the method.

one_liner: Weather shifts do not compose additively: rain+night is worse than rain-effect plus night-effect - measure the interaction matrix.
problem: Robustness studies test single factors (rain OR night OR fog), but deployment presents combinations; if degradations interact super-additively, single-factor benchmarks systematically understate real risk - the interaction structure is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: factorial evaluation over weather-condition combinations reveals significant super-additive interactions for specific pairs (night amplifies rain's effect via reflections; fog amplifies backlight), the interaction matrix is stable across models (physics-driven, not model-driven), and worst-case combinations are predictable from single-factor physics rather than requiring exhaustive testing.
why_important: Safety validation currently extrapolates from single factors; a measured interaction matrix corrects the risk model where it is most wrong.
why_possibly_novel: Factorial interaction analysis of weather robustness is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Use condition-rich datasets (ACDC, BDD) plus controlled synthesis for missing cells, fit interaction terms per class, test cross-model stability.
main_risk: Natural data has sparse combination coverage; synthesis fills cells but needs realism validation.

one_liner: Geometry as the shift-invariant channel: does routing through depth (RGB to depth to segmentation) transfer better than direct RGB segmentation?
problem: Appearance shifts (weather, sensors, geography) barely change scene geometry. If segmentation via an intermediate geometric representation retains more accuracy under shift, the invariance structure of the task itself becomes exploitable - a question about representations, not methods.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a pipeline segmenting from predicted depth+normals (with a thin appearance channel) loses less under photometric/weather shift than matched direct-RGB models (geometry mediates invariance), but pays a measurable in-distribution penalty on texture-defined classes - a quantified invariance-vs-acuity tradeoff with a computable optimal mixing ratio per deployment shift profile.
why_important: Establishes which invariances are worth buying at what acuity price - a design law for robustness rather than another method.
why_possibly_novel: Geometry-mediated transfer quantification for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train matched direct and geometry-mediated segmenters, evaluate across shift ladders, fit the tradeoff frontier and mixing-ratio optimum.
main_risk: Depth estimators carry their own shift sensitivity; measure and account for it explicitly.

one_liner: Benchmark the shift-measures: which unsupervised domain-distance metric actually predicts segmentation performance drop?
problem: Teams estimate deployment risk with feature-space distances (FID-like, MMD, proxy accuracies), but these metrics have never been systematically validated as PREDICTORS of dense-prediction degradation - the meta-question the field skipped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: common distribution distances correlate weakly with segmentation drop across a broad shift matrix (r<0.5), because they weight global appearance over the boundary- and minority-class evidence segmentation depends on; a dense-prediction-specific measure (built from label-free prediction statistics like churn, margin distributions, connected-component statistics) predicts drops substantially better - and the validated predictor becomes a deployment tool.
why_important: Every go/no-go deployment decision under shift implicitly trusts some distance measure; validating them is basic metrological hygiene the field lacks.
why_possibly_novel: Predictive-validity benchmarking of shift measures for dense tasks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Assemble 30+ source-target segmentation pairs with known drops, correlate candidate measures, build and validate the dense-specific predictor.
main_risk: Conclusions depend on shift-pair diversity; deliberately include adversarially-mild and severe pairs.

one_liner: Adaptation hysteresis: a model adapted A-to-B differs from one trained at B directly, and the path-dependence predicts continual-adaptation drift.
problem: Continual test-time adaptation walks models through condition sequences (day to dusk to night). Whether the endpoint depends on the path (hysteresis) - and whether looping conditions returns the model to its start - determines if continual adaptation is stable or secularly drifting.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: adapted models exhibit measurable hysteresis (A-to-B-to-A does not recover the original A performance; the gap grows with loop count - secular drift), drift accumulates in specific layers (normalization and early convolutions), and periodic anchor-replay eliminates it at negligible cost - continual adaptation without anchoring is quantifiably unsafe over long deployments.
why_important: Continual TTA is heading into products; its long-horizon stability has never been characterized, and drift would be a slow silent failure.
why_possibly_novel: Hysteresis/drift analysis of adaptation dynamics is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Cycle models through condition loops (synthetic + ACDC sequences), measure return-gap growth, localize drifting parameters, test anchor-replay.
main_risk: Results depend on the specific TTA algorithm; cover the 3 main families.

one_liner: Annotation-convention shift masquerades as domain shift: cross-country dataset gaps are partly label-sociology gaps.
problem: Cross-dataset evaluation (Cityscapes to IDD to BDD) conflates appearance shift with annotation-convention differences (what counts as 'road' vs 'parking'; curb handling; rider/vehicle splits) - the convention fraction of the measured gap is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: re-annotating a sample of target-domain images under the SOURCE dataset's written protocol recovers a substantial fraction (>25%) of the measured cross-dataset performance gap for affected classes - meaning published cross-domain numbers systematically overstate appearance-driven failure and adaptation methods get credit for learning label conventions.
why_important: Separates two entangled research problems (visual robustness vs ontology mapping) that need entirely different solutions.
why_possibly_novel: Protocol-controlled re-annotation accounting for domain-gap decomposition is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Re-annotate 300 target images under source protocol, re-evaluate the gap per class, tabulate the convention fraction.
main_risk: Written protocols under-specify actual annotator behavior; use annotators trained on source-dataset examples.

one_liner: Resolution regime shift: models trained at 1024px meet 4K deployment - effective receptive fields misalign with object scales in a predictable, correctable way.
problem: Training and deployment resolutions diverge (datasets are downsampled; cameras improve). The resulting scale mismatch between learned receptive fields and presented object sizes is a shift axis handled today by ad hoc resizing folklore.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: performance under resolution shift follows a predictable curve in the ratio of object-pixels-per-receptive-field between train and test, is asymmetric (upscale deployment hurts more than downscale), and optimal test-time resizing is computable from dataset object-size statistics alone - replacing folklore with a scaling rule that recovers most of the mismatch loss.
why_important: Resolution mismatch is ubiquitous and silently mishandled; a validated rule converts a recurring engineering headache into a formula.
why_possibly_novel: Dimensionless resolution-shift law for dense prediction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train at multiple resolutions, test across a resolution ladder, fit the law in ratio coordinates, validate the resizing rule on held-out datasets.
main_risk: Architecture-dependent effects (ViT patchification vs CNN strides) may split the law; fit per family.

one_liner: Compression asymmetry: benchmarks are compressed, deployment streams are rawer - models overfit artifacts they will not see, an inverted shift nobody tests.
problem: Shift studies assume deployment is degraded relative to clean benchmarks, but for compression the arrow can invert: web-scraped training data is heavily compressed while deployment feeds (industrial cameras, medical scanners) are near-lossless - models may DEPEND on compression artifacts.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: models trained on web-compressed data measurably degrade on lossless imagery (artifact dependence: denoising-like artifacts act as learned features), the effect concentrates in texture-defined classes, and light recompression of deployment inputs (deliberately degrading them toward training statistics) IMPROVES accuracy - a counter-intuitive, immediately testable prescription.
why_important: The recompression prescription is deployable in an afternoon if validated; the phenomenon also reframes 'data quality' - matching beats maximizing.
why_possibly_novel: Inverted compression-shift analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Evaluate web-trained models on lossless captures vs recompressed versions of the same, measure the signed effect per class.
main_risk: Effect size may be small for modern diverse training sets; report honestly across training-data eras.

one_liner: Where does foundation-feature robustness come from - data diversity or training objective? Checkpoint-ladder analysis separates the credit.
problem: DINOv2/SAM features transfer robustly, credited vaguely to 'scale'. Whether robustness accrues from data diversity, objective choice, or training duration - decomposable via public checkpoint series - matters for what to invest in next.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: analyzing robustness (shift-retention of downstream segmentation) across public checkpoint ladders and matched-data reruns shows data diversity dominates objective choice by a wide margin (matched-data models converge in robustness across objectives; matched-objective models diverge with data), and robustness saturates earlier in training than in-distribution accuracy - actionable credit assignment for the ecosystem's biggest investment question.
why_important: Billions of compute dollars ride on the diversity-vs-objective question; even partial credit assignment from existing artifacts is high-value.
why_possibly_novel: Robustness credit-assignment via checkpoint forensics is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Probe segmentation robustness across available checkpoint series (DINO variants, MAE, CLIP at multiple data scales), fit robustness-accrual curves per factor where artifacts allow.
main_risk: Public artifacts confound factors; where reruns are needed, use small-scale matched experiments and extrapolate cautiously.

one_liner: Predict per-pixel performance drop from the source model alone: performance forecasting as a first-class dense-prediction task.
problem: Before deployment, teams need per-region risk maps for the target domain without target labels - a forecasting task distinct from adaptation, with no benchmark or standard method for dense prediction.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-pixel drop is forecastable (correlation >0.6 with realized drop) from source-model-computable signals (feature-space distance to training manifold, margin statistics, augmentation sensitivity), forecast errors are themselves structured (over-optimistic on novel classes, over-pessimistic on style variation) - and a benchmark of forecasting quality would expose large differences between signals the field currently treats as interchangeable.
why_important: Risk forecasting is the deployment decision-maker's actual question; formalizing it as a benchmarked task channels research toward what practitioners need.
why_possibly_novel: Dense performance-forecasting benchmark construction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Build forecast-vs-realized evaluation on 10 shift pairs, compare 6 forecasting signals, publish the benchmark protocol.
main_risk: Forecast quality varies by shift type; the benchmark must stratify to avoid misleading averages.

one_liner: Natural adversarial weather mining: search real archives for the worst-case conditions per model, instead of averaging over benchmark weather.
problem: Robustness is reported as averages over available conditions, but safety depends on worst cases; mining large unlabeled archives (webcams, dashcams) for each model's WORST natural conditions - and checking if they are shared across models - is unexplored.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: guided search over unlabeled archives (optimizing a label-free failure proxy) discovers natural condition clusters where model performance is far below benchmark-average robustness numbers (hidden failure modes: specific sun angles, wet-road glare geometries, mixed precipitation), and a substantial fraction of these clusters transfer across model families - natural worst cases are systematic, findable, and shared.
why_important: Averages hide the failures that cause accidents; a mining methodology gives safety teams a repeatable worst-case discovery tool.
why_possibly_novel: Label-free worst-case mining in natural archives for dense prediction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Implement failure-proxy-guided search over webcam archives, verify mined clusters with spot annotation, test cross-model transfer of hardness.
main_risk: Failure proxies may mine proxy-artifacts rather than true failures; spot annotation is the essential control.

one_liner: Time-of-day is a hidden label prior: models learn that parked cars appear at night and fail on time-swapped scenes - anti-causal shortcut measurement.
problem: Class distributions correlate with capture time (delivery trucks by day, parked rows by night); models may encode time-conditioned priors rather than appearance evidence, failing when the correlation breaks (night football game, daytime empty streets).
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: models infer global time-of-day from image statistics and modulate class priors accordingly (probeable: time is linearly decodable from features and causally influences predictions via controlled relighting), and prior-override errors occur at measurable rates on time-atypical scenes - a quantifiable anti-causal shortcut with a stress-test suite as the deliverable.
why_important: Time-atypical scenes (emergencies, events) are exactly when perception must work; a validated stress suite would catch this failure class pre-deployment.
why_possibly_novel: Time-conditioned prior measurement for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Probe time decodability in features, evaluate on curated time-atypical scenes, use relighting interventions to separate appearance from prior effects.
main_risk: Relighting realism; complement with natural time-atypical collections.

one_liner: Per-class transfer matrix of synthetic data: adding simulation helps some real classes and quantifiably harms others - the negative-transfer ledger.
problem: Synthetic data is added wholesale on the assumption of average benefit, but per-class effects (sim vehicles helping, sim pedestrians hurting via uncanny appearance) are rarely itemized - teams cannot make class-level decisions.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: mixed real+synthetic training produces a stable per-class signed-effect ledger (consistent across seeds and architectures), harms concentrate in classes where synthetic appearance diverges most from real (measurable via per-class feature distances), and class-selective synthetic mixing (include only positive-ledger classes) beats wholesale mixing by a meaningful margin - synthetic data needs itemized accounting, not blanket adoption.
why_important: Turns synthetic-data decisions from faith into ledger-driven engineering, with immediate gains from selective mixing.
why_possibly_novel: Signed per-class transfer accounting with selective-mixing validation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train real-only vs mixed vs class-selective mixes on driving data (GTA/SYNTHIA + Cityscapes), tabulate signed ledgers, validate the divergence predictor.
main_risk: Ledger stability across simulators must be tested, not assumed; use two simulators.

one_liner: UDA methods overfit their development benchmark pair: rank correlation across novel shift pairs is the reproducibility number nobody reports.
problem: Unsupervised domain adaptation methods are developed and tuned overwhelmingly on GTA-to-Cityscapes; whether their rankings hold on fresh shift pairs (different domains, modalities, directions) is the field's unasked generalization question about itself.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: re-running leading UDA methods with frozen hyperparameters on 6 novel shift pairs yields low rank correlation with their canonical-benchmark ranking (methods overfit the development pair's shift composition), while simple baselines (strong augmentation, self-training) rank far more stably - the field's method-ranking signal is substantially benchmark-specific noise.
why_important: A meta-scientific audit determining whether UDA progress is real; stability-ranked methods are what practitioners should actually adopt.
why_possibly_novel: Cross-pair rank-stability auditing of UDA is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Reproduce 8 UDA methods, evaluate frozen on novel pairs (medical, aerial, reversed directions), compute rank correlations and stability scores.
main_risk: Frozen hyperparameters may be unfair to methods needing tuning - but that itself is a deployability finding; report both regimes.

one_liner: Metric anchors survive shift: physical size priors (via camera geometry) remain valid when appearance shifts - measure how much of robustness they could carry.
problem: Appearance shifts destroy learned texture cues, but physical regularities (pedestrians ~1.7m, lane widths standardized) survive any weather; how much segmentation robustness metric-scale priors could contribute is unquantified because models entangle scale with appearance.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: probing shows current models' implicit size priors degrade under shift (they are appearance-entangled, not geometric), while models given explicit metric conditioning (camera intrinsics + horizon) retain class discrimination under severe appearance shift measurably better - the shift-invariant information in metric geometry is real, quantifiable, and currently unexploited.
why_important: Identifies an invariance channel that is free at deployment (intrinsics are known) and orthogonal to all appearance-based robustness work.
why_possibly_novel: Metric-prior shift-invariance quantification is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Probe size-prior stability under shift ladders; train matched models with/without metric conditioning; compare shift retention per class.
main_risk: Intrinsics conditioning helps mainly ground-plane-anchored classes; scope claims accordingly.

one_liner: The domain-randomization sweet spot is predictable: too much randomization hurts, and the optimum tracks target-domain variance - fit the curve.
problem: Domain randomization strength is tuned blindly; the community knows extremes fail (too little = overfit, too much = unlearnable invariance) but has no predictive theory of the optimum's location.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: transfer performance vs randomization strength is reliably non-monotonic with a single optimum whose location scales with measured target-domain variance along each factor (color, texture, lighting independently), so the optimal randomization recipe is computable from a small unlabeled target sample - replacing grid search with measurement.
why_important: Randomization tuning consumes large simulation budgets; a predictive rule compresses it to one estimation step, and the variance-matching principle would generalize across factors.
why_possibly_novel: Variance-matched optimal-randomization law is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Sweep per-factor randomization strengths training on synthetic driving data, locate optima across target datasets with different measured variances, test the scaling law.
main_risk: Factor interactions may shift optima jointly; fit both marginal and joint models.

one_liner: Amplitude-swap explains most photometric-shift benefit - but where does PHASE matter? Locate the residual that frequency-domain adaptation cannot touch.
problem: Fourier amplitude transfer between domains is a known cheap adaptation trick (KNOWN: FDA, Yang & Soatto CVPR 2020 - existence confident, details need verification); what remains AFTER amplitude alignment - the phase-borne shift component - has not been characterized, though it defines the method's ceiling.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: after optimal amplitude alignment, residual cross-domain error concentrates in phase-borne structures (layout differences, object-shape variants, edge geometry), is class-structured (things retain more residual than stuff), and no amplitude-space method can reduce it - establishing a measurable decomposition of photometric vs structural shift with amplitude methods' ceiling made explicit.
why_important: Tells the field precisely what the popular cheap trick cannot fix, preventing wasted iterations and directing effort at the structural residual.
why_possibly_novel: Phase-residual characterization of shift is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Apply exhaustive amplitude alignment on 5 shift pairs, decompose residual error by class and spatial-frequency band, compare against phase-perturbation sensitivity curves.
main_risk: Amplitude/phase decomposition is a linear-systems view of a nonlinear problem; treat as first-order analysis and validate conclusions behave stably.

one_liner: Part of every 'domain gap' is an annotation-quality gap: target-domain labels are often worse, inflating measured shift.
problem: Cross-domain evaluation assumes both domains' labels are equally good, but target datasets (developing-region driving data, rare-modality medical sets) often have younger annotation pipelines - measured 'domain gaps' partially reflect reference-quality differences.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: expert re-annotation of target-domain test samples to source-grade quality reduces measured domain gaps by a nontrivial fraction (>15% of the gap for at least some benchmark pairs), and the label-quality component is diagnosable WITHOUT re-annotation via model-consensus statistics - separating true shift from reference noise in every cross-domain claim.
why_important: Domain-gap numbers steer research priorities and product decisions; systematically inflated gaps misdirect both.
why_possibly_novel: Reference-quality decomposition of measured domain gaps is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Re-annotate 200 target test images at source-grade for 2 benchmark pairs, recompute gaps, validate the consensus-based diagnostic against realized corrections.
main_risk: Which pairs have quality asymmetry is unknown a priori; survey with the diagnostic first, then re-annotate the flagged pairs.

one_liner: Camera height is a geometric shift solvable in closed form: dashcam-to-bodycam transfer needs homography priors, not learned adaptation.
problem: Viewpoint-height shift (vehicle roof vs handheld vs robot-dog height) is treated with generic adaptation machinery, though it is substantially a known geometric transformation of ground-plane layout - suggesting geometry should replace learning for this axis.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for height shifts, ground-plane homography-based training augmentation (exact geometric reprojection given height priors) recovers more of the cross-height performance gap than generic UDA methods at a fraction of the complexity, and the residual after geometric correction isolates the truly appearance-borne component (occlusion pattern changes) - geometry-first decomposition beats learning-first for geometrically-caused shifts.
why_important: A class of shifts where the right answer is 100-year-old projective geometry would recalibrate the learn-everything reflex, with immediate value for robot/drone deployment from vehicle-collected data.
why_possibly_novel: Geometric-vs-learned adaptation head-to-head for height shift is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Construct height-paired data (multi-mount captures or synthetic), compare homography augmentation vs 3 UDA methods on cross-height segmentation.
main_risk: Homography assumes planar ground; cluttered 3D scenes violate it - measure where the assumption breaks.
